title: Multi-region failover coordinator: graceful quiesce, circuit-breaker gating, and fallback variant mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a coordinator service and readiness checks that enable low-risk multi-region failovers. This ticket covers: 1) a 'quiesce' protocol to gracefully drain traffic and complete in-flight KV/cache priming work, 2) a circuit-breaker gating layer to avoid thundering herd during failovers, 3) deterministic mapping rules that select fallback model variants by region and tier, and 4) a lightweight scoreboard and handshake to assert warm-standby readiness before traffic cutover. Motivation: incidents where sudden cutover caused cache misses and model-variant mismatches leading to latency spikes and degraded outputs. Success is a measurable reduction in failover tail latency and fewer SLO violations during cutovers.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator exposes readiness endpoint with 3-level status: GREEN (ready), YELLOW (partial readiness), RED (not ready).
Automated cutover robot waits for GREEN or YELLOW+acceptance-policy before shifting >20% traffic; default policy: require GREEN or 3 continuous minutes of YELLOW with kv-prefetch >= 85%.
Circuit-breaker prevents >2 concurrent region activations per tenant and enforces backoff ramp for downstream caches to avoid global stampede.
Fallback variant mapping resolves to compatible quantization/profile and runtime kernel set; integration tests validate functional parity for 95% of evaluation prompts.
End-to-end simulation (chaos run) shows <10% increase in p99 latency during a full-region failover compared to baseline and no regression in generation quality (ROUGE-like threshold).
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature flag under /routing/coordinator; unit + integration tests in CI; small-canary: enable for internal tenant only. Phase 2: Canary across 3 low-traffic customer accounts with synthetic traffic and real prompt evals. Phase 3: Gradual ramp across regions with traffic-shaping and telemetry gating. Rollback via feature-flag off and automated re-route to origin region. Estimated time: 2 weeks of canary + 1 week of ramp.
mitigation_playbook: If coordinator returns RED: block activation and keep traffic pinned to active region; trigger on-call page.
If circuit-breaker trips unexpectedly: mark region as degraded and redirect to next-priority region; trigger telemetry alert for investigation.
If model-variant mismatch detected: fall back to next-compatible variant and schedule async model warm-up; notify SRE and ML Ops.
design_decisions: Use a small, independent coordinator microservice (stateless leader for a region) rather than embedding logic into the router to simplify rollbacks and observability.

Readiness calculation includes three signals: (1) KV cache hit rate for synthetic priming queries, (2) model instance health and kernel compatibility probe, (3) network egress/connectivity checks to critical infra (KMS, control plane).
Fallback mapping is deterministic ordered list per region: preferred model -> lower-cost quantized variant -> cross-region replica. We avoid live model conversion during cutover to reduce unknowns.
tradeoffs: Pro: Independent coordinator allows feature-flagged testing and fine-grained telemetry. Con: extra service increases operational surface area and slight routing latency (~2-4ms).
Pro: Strict readiness gates reduce SLO risk. Con: may delay failover in severely degraded but functional scenarios; mitigated by YELLOW acceptance policy.
Pro: Deterministic fallback reduces surprises. Con: might not pick most cost-optimal variant in some edge workloads; we allow per-tenant overrides.
tests: Unit tests for quiesce handshake and timeout semantics.
Integration test that simulates region drain with 10k concurrent in-flight requests and validates KV rehydration thresholds.
Chaos test in staging: tombstone region and run full cutover while checking p50/p95/p99 and quality metrics.
E2E canary with real traffic on internal tenant and manual quality review for outlier prompts.
